answers.final_answer: Net exports will increase, and real GDP will increase.
answers.brief_reasoning: Depreciation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer, so net exports rise. That raises aggregate demand, which increases real GDP in the short run.
When the currency depreciates, the country's goods and assets get cheaper for foreigners. They buy more of them, so they need more of the currency, which is why quantity demanded rises.
